In Ottawa, Canada, and feeling pretty desperate.

I’m really sorry you’re in this spot. Let’s get practical — you need $200 by Sunday night in Ottawa. Here are the most realistic ways to get cash fast, even with no job and nothing to sell.

### 1. Donate plasma — real cash, same day
In Ottawa, **Canadian Plasma Resources** pays donors. It’s not blood donation — it’s plasma, and private clinics in Canada are allowed to compensate you.

- Search **“Canadian Plasma Resources Ottawa”** and call the location on **Carling Avenue**.
- New donors can often make **$50–$100 per donation**, and sometimes there are bonuses for the first few visits.
- You need **government ID**, and you should **eat well and drink water** beforehand.
- The first donation takes a few hours, but you can get paid after.

If you can get $100 from plasma, you’re halfway there.

### 2. Pawn or sell something you own
You said you have nothing to sell, but do you have:
- A smartphone? (Even an older one can get $100–$200)
- A laptop, tablet, gaming console, bike, winter jacket, camera, tools, or jewelry?

Pawnshops in Ottawa are open on Sundays. You can pawn an item and get cash immediately. If you can get your rent paid, you can always try to get the item back later. It’s not ideal, but it’s better than being on the street.

### 3. Offer “same-day labour” on Kijiji and Facebook
Post in Ottawa community groups, Kijiji, and Facebook Marketplace:

> “Available TODAY. I’ll do yard work, moving help, furniture assembly, cleaning, junk removal, painting, or any physical labour. $25–$30/hour. Need cash today. Can start immediately.”

Also check Kijiji under **“Gigs”** and **“Odd Jobs”** — people post same-day moving help, house cleaning, dog walking, etc.

You can also stand outside a **Home Depot or Rona** with a sign that says “Available for work today” — contractors sometimes pick people up for cash jobs.

### 4. Collect bottles and cans
In Ontario, beer bottles, wine bottles, and liquor bottles have deposits. You can go around apartment buildings, parks, and recycling bins in areas like **ByWard Market, Sandy Hill, Lowertown, and Hintonburg** and collect bottles.

It’s not glamorous, and it’s a lot of work, but you can turn in bottles at **The Beer Store** for cash. If you hit enough recycling bins, you can make $50–$100. It won’t get you the full $200, but combined with plasma, it can get you close.

### 5. Busk or panhandle in ByWard Market
If you have any musical talent, go to **ByWard Market** or **Rideau Street** and play. If you don’t, you can still stand with a sign that says:

> “Student short on rent. Anything helps. Thank you.”

It’s humiliating, but it works. People in Ottawa are generally kind, and on a Sunday in ByWard Market, you can make $50–$150 if you stay for several hours.

### 6. Ask your landlord for a one-day extension and offer to work it off
You said your landlord is already pissed, but you can try:

> “I have $X right now. I’m trying to get the rest by tomorrow night. Can I pay $200 on Monday and also do some work around the building to show good faith?”

Sometimes landlords are more willing if you offer something extra. It’s not guaranteed, but it’s worth a shot.

### 7. Avoid payday loans
I know you’re desperate, but payday loans will make things worse. They charge insane interest and you’ll be in a deeper hole next month. Same with loan sharks. Don’t do it.

---

### Your best plan for Sunday:
- **Morning:** Go to Canadian Plasma Resources and donate plasma. Try to get $100.
- **Afternoon:** Post on Kijiji/Facebook for same-day labour and hit recycling bins for bottles.
- **Evening:** If you’re still short, pawn something or go to ByWard Market and ask for help.

You can do this. It’s going to be a long, shitty day, but you can get $200 together. Good luck.
